newsitem.title: USA: N.J. unemployment rate falls to 5.5 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: N.J. unemployment rate falls to 5.5 pct in March.

text.p: New Jersey's unemployment rate dropped in March to 5.5 percent on a seasonally-adjusted basis from a revised 5.6 percent in February, the state's Department of Labor said Friday.
The number of people employed in the state rose 4,000 from February, to 3.7 million in March, the department said.

"Since January 1994, New Jersey has had a net gain of 180,400 jobs," Labor Commissioner Mel Gelade said in a statement announcing the figures. "The addition in March of 4,000 means that more workers were on the job in New Jersey than at any time since September 1989."
Department analysts said some workers found jobs in March due to better-than-usual winter weather, which may result in some dampening of the figures for the Spring.
The survey also found that the workweek of production workers in New Jersey's factories rose over the month by 0.1 hour to 42 hours in March.
